title: Finite-sample density reconstruction from a single causal order
description:
We observe only the isomorphism class of the strict coordinatewise order of n independent points in the unit square. Their unknown density is smooth, lies between 1/2 and 3/2, has uniform marginals, and is Euclidean Lipschitz with constant at most two. We construct one measurable order-only estimator whose full-square supremum error, modulo one global coordinate exchange, is at most min{1/2,650(log n/n)^(1/4)} with probability at least 19/20, uniformly over this original class and for every n at least 2.

The main reduction uses observed predecessor and successor counts: every retained point has reliable reconstructed coordinates, while every point needed in sufficiently deep cells is retained. This removes a global discarded-mass penalty from local estimation. The paper gives complete proofs, including attributed earlier geometric forcing, an actual single-n order-law inverse corollary, and smooth marginal-preserving Gaussian alternatives. For n at least 16, every estimator, including independent randomization and with measurable success events, has strict error greater than n^(-1/4)/6 with probability greater than 1/4 under an admissible density. The explicit all-n finite risk and random-width-band qualification are also given.

The upper, law and randomized lower endpoints have exact-source Lean 4 acceptance on remote GCP. The shared proof library audit covers 446 selected exports; this is not a count of this paper's results. This is a theory result with conservative constants, a selector using finite classical choices and an uninformative frozen practical pilot. The lower bound already holds with coordinate data. The logarithmic gap, efficient implementation and useful practical calibration remain unresolved; no additional order-information cost, exact minimax rate or mathematical priority is claimed.

Author: Daniel Eric Fredriksen, Quantyra Inc. Developed with OpenAI Codex assistance. Review is open-source, decentralized and informal, through inspectable proofs, reuse and downstream testing. Manuscript: CC-BY-4.0. The source archive includes the reviewed preparation snapshot and publication edition; the separately linked proof software and reused repository publication helpers retain Apache-2.0 licensing. This is a third manuscript family, distinct from the reconstruction and coordinate-gauge papers sharing its proof repository.
